title: Verb patterns: gerund and infinitive
tagline: The verb right before decides the form: -ing, to + infinitive, or the infinitive with no 'to' at all.
exam: Reading & Use of English Part 4 — key word transformations
Reading & Use of English Part 3 — word formation and multiple-choice cloze
why: A handful of very common verbs — remember, forget, stop, try, regret, mean, go on — change meaning completely depending on whether they're followed by -ing or a to-infinitive. B2 First tests this directly, and getting it wrong doesn't just cost a mark: it changes what the sentence says.

rows.label: + -ing
cells: a past action you recall (or don't) doing
an activity ends — it stops happening

rows.label: + to-infinitive
cells: a task you need to do, before or after
you pause to do something else instead
make an effort at something difficult

rows.label: Example
cells: I remember locking the door. / Remember to lock the door.
She stopped eating meat. / She stopped to eat lunch.
Try restarting the laptop. / Try to finish on time.

diagrams.title: make / let + bare infinitive
diagrams.caption: Miss Vega let us leave early after the test.

head: Pattern
Meaning change?
Example
rows: Sofia avoids meeting new people on the first day.
Liam managed to finish the project on time.
start / begin / continue / love / hate + -ing or to-
It started raining. / It started to rain.
I remember locking the door. / Don't forget to lock it.
yes — what stops vs what's next
He stopped smoking. / He stopped to smoke.
Try restarting the router. / Try to stay calm.
It was hard to concentrate during the storm.
Her parents let her go to the concert.

examples.text: Nadia can't imagine living anywhere other than Arequipa.
I'd avoid mentioning the exam results if I were you — Liam's upset.

use.point: Verbs that only take a to-infinitive

examples.text: Sofia decided to apply for the summer exchange programme.
We finally managed to book the tickets before they sold out.

use.point: Verbs that change meaning with -ing or to-infinitive

examples.text: I clearly remember switching off the lights before we left.
examples.note: a past action I recall doing

examples.text: Please remember to switch off the lights when you leave.
Liam stopped checking his phone during dinner — finally.
We stopped to check the map halfway up the trail.
examples.note: paused an activity in order to do something else

examples.text: Nadia is interested in studying marine biology after school.
The teacher let the class choose their own topics this term.

watch_out.wrong: I enjoy to read before bed.
watch_out.why: Enjoy is always followed by -ing, never a to-infinitive.
Decide is always followed by a to-infinitive, never -ing.

watch_out.wrong: I'll never forget to visit Machu Picchu for the first time.
watch_out.right: I'll never forget visiting Machu Picchu for the first time.
watch_out.why: A past memory takes -ing; forget to means a task you didn't do.

watch_out.wrong: He stopped to smoke ten years ago, and he's never gone back.
watch_out.right: He stopped smoking ten years ago, and he's never gone back.
watch_out.why: The habit itself ending needs -ing, not to-infinitive.

watch_out.wrong: My parents let me to stay out later on Fridays.
watch_out.right: My parents let me stay out later on Fridays.
watch_out.why: Let is followed by the bare infinitive — never add to.

watch_out.wrong: It's important arriving on time for the mock exam.
watch_out.right: It's important to arrive on time for the mock exam.
watch_out.why: Adjective + to-infinitive is the fixed pattern, not -ing.

dialogue.title: Revising for the mock exam
dialogue.context: Nadia and Mateo are comparing study habits before the B2 First mock exam, with Miss Vega checking in.

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: I really need to finish the reading paper tonight — I keep putting it off.

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: Same. I tried studying after dinner yesterday, but I fell asleep on the sofa.

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: Try doing it earlier then. Have you finished revising the reported speech unit?

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: Almost. I remember struggling with that one in class, so I'm going over it again.

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: Don't forget to check the listening scripts too — I found them really useful.

lines.speaker: Miss Vega
lines.text: Good habits, both of you. I'd recommend practising under timed conditions before Friday.

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: We will. Actually, could you let us see last year's paper again?

lines.speaker: Miss Vega
lines.text: I can email it tonight — just remind me if I forget.

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: We won't stop you forgetting — Mateo already set two reminders.

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: I plan to sleep properly this week too. No more studying until midnight.

items.sentence: Sofia suggested ___ the museum before the trip ends.
Liam hopes ___ the football team next season.
I clearly remember ___ the door before we left the house.
items.why: a memory of a completed action = -ing

items.sentence: We stopped ___ photos at the viewpoint before continuing the walk.
items.why: paused the walk in order to take photos

items.sentence: Her coach let her ___ the training session early.
It was impossible ___ during the storm last night.
Mateo is thinking ___ a new laptop before the school year starts.

practice.instructions: Complete each sentence with the correct form of the verb in brackets.

items.sentence: Nadia finally managed ___ (finish) the essay just before the deadline.
I really enjoy ___ (listen) to podcasts on the way to school.
Please remember ___ (bring) your ID card for the exam tomorrow.
He stopped ___ (check) his phone every five minutes — it was driving everyone mad.
Try ___ (explain) it more slowly; maybe that will help.
The teacher made us ___ (rewrite) the whole paragraph.
Sofia is interested in ___ (study) marine biology after school.
We can't afford ___ (miss) any more classes before the exam.

practice.instructions: Complete the second sentence so that it has a similar meaning to the first. Use the word given. Do not change it. Use between two and five words.

items.first: Liam didn't manage to finish the report on time.
I have a clear memory of switching off the lights.
Don't forget: you need to bring your passport tomorrow.
Her parents allowed her to stay out until midnight.
Nadia paused her homework in order to answer the phone.
It isn't easy to concentrate with all this noise.

summary: The verb before decides the form: some verbs (enjoy, avoid, finish) always take -ing; others (decide, hope, manage) always take to-infinitive.
Remember, forget, stop and try change meaning: -ing looks at a past or ongoing action, to-infinitive looks at a task still to do.
Start, begin, continue, love and hate accept either form with little or no change in meaning.
Adjectives are usually followed by a to-infinitive; prepositions are always followed by -ing.
Make and let are followed by the bare infinitive — never add 'to' after them.
